learning_path.goal: Understand how Kong durably broadcasts a cluster event and delivers it once to remote-node subscribers despite polling intervals, delays, pagination, worker concurrency, and failures.

start_here.reason: The reviewed trace begins in cluster_events/init.lua because it selects the strategy and owns broadcast, subscription, shared state, polling, delivery, error handling, and recurring scheduling.

learning_path.trace: Start with new selecting a strategy, server-time cursor, node identity and shared-memory state; follow broadcast into durable insertion, subscribe into polling startup, then poll through concurrency locks, lookback cursor, paged database selection, cursor advancement, same-node suppression, shared-memory deduplication, not-before delay, protected callbacks, error handling, cleanup, and recurring timer scheduling; close the lifecycle in the dedicated cluster-events integration suite.

signals: metatable modules and strategy polymorphism
iterator-based database pagination and callback registries
OpenResty timers, shared dictionaries, protected calls, and concurrency helpers
language_technique.reason: Substantial framework and runtime abstractions shape the path without pervasive expert Lua metaprogramming.

signals: durable publish, recurring poll, shared cursor, lookback, pagination, deduplication, delayed delivery, callback, and cleanup state interact
multiple nodes and workers race through database time, local time, shared memory, locks, timers, and same-node suppression
database, timer, lock, cursor-eviction, callback, scheduling, and shutdown failures require distinct recovery behavior
behavioral_reasoning.reason: Several advanced distributed, concurrent, scheduled, persistent, and recovery concerns interact pervasively.

signals: cluster-event public API and channel registry
PostgreSQL and off persistence strategies
database connector, node identity, OpenResty workers, shared memory, locks, timers, clock, and integration-test subsystems
design_span.reason: The selected behavior coordinates several major runtime, persistence, process, and platform subsystems.

signals: events must not be lost, replayed incorrectly, delivered to the publishing node, duplicated across workers, or observed before not-before time
database and local clocks, lookback, TTL, cursor eviction, polling interval, delay, page boundaries, locks, and shared-memory expiration interact
a local change can break cluster convergence, callback isolation, database load, worker liveness, upgrade compatibility, reliability, or performance
constraint_burden.reason: Several system-wide correctness, liveness, durability, timing, recovery, compatibility, and performance guarantees require expert change discipline.

learning_level.placement: The four scores 3/5/5/5 sum to 18; their arithmetic mean is 4.50 and rounds half-up to Level 5. The published result is Level 5.

quality.source_quality: cluster_events/init.lua keeps validation, strategy selection, cursors, locks, pagination, lookback, suppression, deduplication, delays, callbacks, cleanup, and timer recovery explicit.
quality.architecture: The public cluster-events API composes a persistence strategy with database time, shared worker state, concurrency locks, recurring timers, channel subscribers, and protected callback delivery.
quality.naming_and_idiom: cluster_events, broadcast, subscribe, poll, postgres and off strategies, node identity, lookback, not-before time, and shared cursors make distributed lifecycle intent visible.
quality.tests: 01-cluster_events_spec.lua covers singleton construction, node identity, polling startup, broadcast, remote delivery, same-node suppression, lookback, pagination, callback errors, and delay.
quality.documentation: README.md and DEVELOPER.md orient Kong's node and development environment sufficiently for the bounded cluster-events subsystem.
quality.traceability: An event can be followed from broadcast and database insertion through a locked polling page, cursor and deduplication checks, delayed callback, and dedicated integration assertions.
quality.maintainability: Persistence strategies, concurrency helpers, and time helpers isolate runtime contracts, while one direct integration suite protects cross-node and cross-worker behavior.
quality.educational_value: The path provides a representative production lesson in distributed event delivery without requiring Kong's proxy, router, plugin, and PDK breadth.
